class.name: LocalMultiplayerPeer
class.brief_description: An in-process [MultiplayerPeer] that routes packets through memory.
class.description: No socket is opened. Peer IDs, connection status and packet queues answer exactly what [ENetMultiplayerPeer]'s do, so a [MultiplayerAPI] cannot tell which one it is holding, and a test drives a real session without a network. [codeblock] var server := LocalMultiplayerPeer.new() var client := LocalMultiplayerPeer.new() server.create_server() client.create_client(42) server.force_connect_peer(42, client) client.force_connect_peer(1, server) [/codeblock] The links form a star and not a mesh: a client is linked to the server and to nobody else, so a packet addressed to another client reaches the server for relaying and costs a second poll. Connection events are queued and emitted on [method MultiplayerPeer.poll], which is what makes them land at a point the caller chose. Setting [member loopback_session] gives that session first refusal on every inbound packet, so [LocalLinkConditions] can hold or drop one before it is ever visible here.

method.name: create_client
method.description: Initializes this peer as a client with [param client_id]. The peer reports [constant MultiplayerPeer.CONNECTION_CONNECTING] until its first [method MultiplayerPeer.poll].

method.name: create_server
method.description: Initializes this peer as the server, whose id is always [code]1[/code].

method.name: force_connect_peer
method.description: Records [param peer] as reachable under [param peer_id]. On the server side this also queues the [signal MultiplayerPeer.peer_connected] that the next [method MultiplayerPeer.poll] emits.

method.name: is_linked_to
method.description: Returns whether [param peer_id] is currently reachable from this peer.

method.name: linked_peer_ids
method.description: Returns every reachable peer id, in the order they were linked.

members.member: The [LocalLoopbackSession] that conditions this peer's inbound traffic. It is held weakly, so it never keeps a session alive.
